scientific_question: Does the paper's low-data FT claim survive a strict group-split, three-seed comparison for both 600 K and Multi-T data?
definition: Five percent of periodic training configurations, sampled within each training source trajectory; valid/test unchanged; three isolated-atom E0 anchors retained.

selection.isolated_atom_policy: retain all isolated anchors outside the periodic-frame fraction
selection.valid_test_policy: copy unchanged from the full grouped release
selection.reason: Global frame sampling is reproducible but can underrepresent a source trajectory; stratification preserves coverage while keeping the split units fixed.

model_matrix.foundation_role: same OMAT checkpoint for all six models

acceptance_gates: generated train/valid/test hashes and counts match a frozen selection manifest
all source trajectories remain confined to one split
all six jobs use the same foundation hash, architecture, optimizer, and data-release protocol within family
seed, job ID, environment, checkpoints, compiled model, and model hash are recorded
all models load and produce finite Cr/Sb/Te energies and forces
test RMSE is reported separately for each family and seed
the 5% claim is compared against full-data grouped controls, not historical random-split models
publication_boundary: Until all six models pass the acceptance gates, this is a training campaign, not evidence that 5% data matches full-data performance.
